summary:
**Proposal: QUARANTINE.** Root keeps the fail-closed gate. This is not reviewer approval, not scoped-lab promotion, and not a production release.

The packet is internally consistent and the protocol is real: preregistered 18/12/24 split, six synthetic families, three arms, counterbalanced order, 128-token cap, 108 local calls and 3,725 generated tokens, full request/output logs, independent scoring, UCB fit only on development then frozen, no weight updates. 54×3 = 162 saved outputs regenerating in a fresh process, and an exact snapshot restore, show the harness and the frozen artifact replay. They do not show fresh model inference. The preregistered 6-case live reproduction (first critical case per category) is still unrun. Cached replay is the wrong evidence for a status upgrade.

Holdout shared-outcome replay, 24 tasks: fixed direct 12/24, random 16/24, greedy and UCB both 23/24, fixed deterministic tools 24/24, fixed one-model-plus-tool team 24/24. The learning-disabled ablation equals fixed direct at 12/24, so the 11-task gap versus direct is tied to learned arm choice inside this suite, not to tools merely being present. Greedy tying UCB means the packet does not separate the UCB bonus from greedy. The paired delta versus direct is 0.458 (95% percentile bootstrap [0.25, 0.667], n=24). That interval is descriptive only: tasks are repeats of six templates, about four holdout rows per family, so one template can mint several “successes.” Validation scores are not in the packet. No per-family table is in the packet.

**Limited policy adaptation.** Supported only as a within-suite, development-frozen, descriptive finding against fixed direct, random, and the learning-off ablation, on this digest (`a4564677…db150c`) and these synthetic families. Not supported as a policy to install, even in a named lab route. One more live draw, one new surface form, or one family where the tool is wrong can erase a gap built from correlated templates.

**Deterministic baseline dominates** on the reported holdout quality score: tools and the fixed team both go 24/24; UCB goes 23/24. The cost line (candidate 586 tokens / 7.657 s versus fixed 1,053 tokens / 11.784 s, 24 calls) is a win against fixed direct only. Tool-only model-token cost is not reported. UCB still spent 586 generated tokens to land one success short of the arm that does not need those tokens. The 128-token cap can favor short tool answers; mean length (~34.5 tokens) shows the cap did not hit every call, but it remains a designed bias. “No critical or category regression versus direct” uses the weak arm as the bar.

**Do not** treat this as general superiority, production deployment, or a reason to edit frozen weights or prompts after holdout. Any post-holdout prompt or weight change invalidates the split.

**Next falsifiable hypothesis, unchanged artifact.** On a fresh process, same digest, restored snapshot, no prompt or weight edits, the six preregistered critical cases match the stored arm and the stored independent score on every case. Fail if any score or chosen arm differs. Only if that passes: a new preregistered slice, same frozen policy, five families left well-specified and one family with the deterministic tool intentionally wrong. Predict tools stay at least tied with UCB on the five well-specified families. A win only on the broken family does not license adaptation.
